copy.blurb:
A +7.5pp gap on the South Africa side. Mexico v South Africa in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has South Africa stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Public Elo rates Mexico 210 points higher than the other side (Mexico 1830, South Africa 1620). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Mexico to win at 64%, the draw at 17%, and South Africa to win at 19%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Mexico to win at 68%, the draw at 20%, and South Africa to win at 11%. On the South Africa side specifically the market reads 11%, which prices out at American odds of +780. Compared against the model's 19%, that's the +7.5pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On South Africa the lower bound is 15%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.8pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 10 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read. Per Al Jazeera English: "The warm-up friendly simulated World Cup conditions, including cooling breaks for the players, at the Rose Bowl stadium." Yahoo Sports (soccer) carried the same line: "FIFA has imposed a last-minute sanction on the Mexican National Team due to repeated incidents of the discriminatory chant."
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the South Africa side still clears the Pick threshold.
